skill.name: sql-query-builder
skill.description: Build SQL from plain-language requests, then review execution-plan concerns and optimization options.
skill.summary: Create SQL queries with execution-plan analysis and practical optimization guidance.
skill.author: Hermes-Sedimentary

security_audit.summary: The high-entropy static finding is a false positive. SKILL.md is readable Markdown with front matter and short SQL assistant documentation, not binary or encrypted content. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or hidden execution behavior was found.

static_findings.pattern: [HEURISTIC] High file entropy (6.28 bits) - possible binary/encrypted content

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md is a 34-line readable Markdown file with YAML front matter and plain Chinese feature text. The entropy signal appears caused by multilingual text and symbols, not binary, encrypted, or obfuscated content.

content.user_title: Build SQL Queries From Plain Language
content.value_statement: Teams often spend time turning data questions into reliable SQL. This skill converts plain language into SQL guidance with execution-plan review and optimization advice.
actual_capabilities: Converts natural-language data requests into SQL query guidance.
Reviews likely execution-plan concerns for generated or existing queries.
Suggests optimization ideas for indexes, filters, joins, and query shape.
Supports conversational use in Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
Reminds users to review important database output before use.
limitations: It does not document a live database connection or automatic query execution.
It cannot infer private schemas unless the user provides table details.
Generated SQL should be reviewed before production use.
Dialect-specific behavior depends on the database context supplied by the user.

use_cases.title: Create Reporting Queries
use_cases.description: Turn business questions into draft SQL for metrics, grouped summaries, and filtered reports.

use_cases.title: Improve Slow Queries
use_cases.description: Review an existing query and get practical ideas for plan analysis and optimization.

use_cases.title: Prepare Database Tasks
use_cases.description: Draft query approaches before asking a database owner to validate schema details and access rules.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Basic Query
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a plain business question and known table names.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a SQL query for this request: [describe the data question]. Use these tables and columns: [schema details]. Explain any assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt to a Database Dialect
prompt_templates.scenario: Add database-specific context for better syntax choices.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a [PostgreSQL/MySQL/SQLite/SQL Server] query for this request: [goal]. Use this schema: [schema]. Note dialect-specific choices.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Existing Query
prompt_templates.scenario: Check a draft query before running it on important data.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this SQL query for correctness, performance risks, and missing filters: [paste query]. Use this schema context: [schema details].

prompt_templates.title: Plan an Optimized Query
prompt_templates.scenario: Use known data size and access patterns for deeper optimization.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an optimized query for this workload: [goal]. Include likely execution-plan concerns, index suggestions, and tradeoffs for large tables.

output_examples.input: Find monthly revenue by region from orders and customers.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a grouped query approach, explains required joins, and notes indexes that may help date and region filters.

output_examples.input: Review a slow customer activity query before production use.
output_examples.output: The skill highlights likely scan and join risks, suggests filter changes, and lists schema details needed for a safer final query.

output_examples.input: Create a PostgreSQL query for active subscriptions ending this month.
output_examples.output: The skill drafts PostgreSQL-oriented SQL guidance, states assumptions about status fields, and recommends validation against real table definitions.

best_practices: Provide table names, column names, relationships, and database dialect before asking for SQL.
Ask for assumptions and edge cases when queries affect reporting or billing.
Validate generated SQL on safe test data before using it in production.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for production-ready SQL without sharing schema details.
Do not run generated queries against sensitive data without review.
Do not rely on optimization advice without checking real execution plans.

faq.question: Can this skill connect to my database?
faq.answer: No live database connection is documented. It helps draft and review SQL based on the context you provide.

faq.question: Which database systems does it support?
faq.answer: It can guide SQL for common databases when you specify the dialect. Exact syntax depends on the details you provide.

faq.question: Can it optimize slow queries?
faq.answer: It can suggest likely optimization ideas and execution-plan concerns. You should confirm them with real database plans.

faq.question: Does it replace a database administrator?
faq.answer: No. It is an AI assistant for drafting and review. Important changes still need expert validation.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should I include in my prompt?
faq.answer: Include the data goal, table names, column names, relationships, database dialect, and performance constraints.
